# Ledger 1.3

Ledger 1.3 lets you preview an import, imports each payment once, and reads Alfa-Bank exports without setup.
It also takes larger files and says which columns a rejected file is missing.

## Update Bun before you update Ledger

Ledger 1.3 needs Bun 1.2 or later.
To see which version you have, run `bun --version`.
If the version is older than 1.2, run `bun upgrade`.

## Preview an import before it changes your books

To see what an import would add, run `bun run import --dry-run <file>`.
Ledger lists the transactions the import would add and writes nothing to `ledger.csv`.
When the list looks right, run the same command without `--dry-run`.

## Import each payment once

Ledger 1.2 imported a payment twice when its payee name differed only in spaces or letter case, such as `"Coffee Shop"` and `" coffee shop "`.
Ledger 1.3 imports that payment once.
Two transactions now count as one payment when they have the same date, the same amount to the cent, and the same payee.
Before it compares payees, Ledger removes the spaces at the start and end of each name and changes every letter to lowercase.

## Import Alfa-Bank exports as they are

Ledger 1.3 reads an Alfa-Bank export as the bank produces it.
You no longer need a column mapping for Alfa-Bank in `ledger.config.json`.

## Import files up to 50 MB

Each file you import can now be up to 50 MB.
The limit in Ledger 1.2 was 10 MB.

## Find the columns a rejected file is missing

When a file lacks columns that Ledger needs, Ledger stops with the error `MISSING_COLUMNS`.
In Ledger 1.3, that error names each missing column.
